title: The Great Discourse on Traces Left Behind (DN14)
altTitles: The Great Discourse on Traces Left Behind
dateDisplay: Composed c. 4th–2nd centuries BCE; written down in the 1st century BCE
author: buddha
attributionNote: The discourse is presented in the canonical collection as the Buddha's teaching, transmitted by the early Buddhist community. Authorship of the surviving Pali text is collective and anonymous.
description: The Great Discourse on Traces Left Behind is sutta 14 of the Dīgha Nikāya (Long Discourses). The Long Discourses collect thirty-four suttas of the Pali canon, including the Brahmajāla, the Sāmaññaphala and the Mahāparinibbāna. They are preserved in Pali and translated here by Bhikkhu Sujato.
historicalContext: The Dīgha Nikāya belongs to the Sutta Piṭaka of the Theravada canon. The discourses were transmitted orally and written down in Sri Lanka in the first century BCE; the collection as it survives reflects that transmission.
